# ADR-047a — Amendment to ADR-047: a provider-side deletion marker (`deleted_at`) is reconciliation, not deletion; hot sync never tombstones

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Amendment to ADR-047 (2026-08-25, Checkpoint 6.3, user-approved): a provider-side deletion marker is reconciliation, not local data destruction.** ADR-047's prohibition stands in full for what it was written about: **automatic physical deletion, expiration and retention pruning of health data remain forbidden**, and any retention policy is still a separate, explicitly-approved decision. Distinct from that: setting a **soft, reversible `deleted_at` marker** on a health session that the provider itself no longer returns is reconciliation with upstream truth -- the row is retained indefinitely and nothing is pruned. It is permitted **only** under every one of these conditions simultaneously: `external_key_source = 'data_point_name'` (a stable provider resource name -- derived-key sessions are **never** tombstoned, mirroring the caution already applied to raw heart rate); a **fully fetched, authoritative** warm or manual window; and a **non-empty `seenKeys`** set. **Hot sync never tombstones.** Reappearance clears `deleted_at`, so the marker is reversible in both directions. This confirms and scopes the earlier user decision to tombstone only stable name-keyed sessions. ADR-047's other clauses -- daily aggregates plus sessions, intraday for `heart-rate` alone, metric-implied units, and the structural true-zero/missing distinction -- are unchanged
